rv.q: If the show still works, it is largely because it boasts one of Lloyd Webber’s best, most tightly composed scores.

Kenwright and his co-director Bob Tomson have steeped themselves in this score and their polished account teases out nuggets of subtext at every turn, abetted on this occasion by the devastatingly good Eva of Madalena Alberto .
For my part, it is the worst production of a musical I have ever seen on a West End stage.

cn.t: Critics are divided on this Evita revival: while some praise Madalena Alberto's performance and the elegant production design, others find it underwhelming, with sound issues undermining Tim Rice's lyrics.
